record.narrative: This first proposal set focuses on direct, biologically motivated dependencies in a lung cancer cell line panel, while also testing a co-mutation interaction and one constructed marker. The strongest a priori claims are pathway-specific: KRAS-mutant cells should be more strongly dependent on KRAS; BRAF V600E-mutant cells should be more strongly dependent on BRAF; amplified receptor tyrosine kinases should show enhanced dependency on EGFR or ERBB2; MSI-high cells should show WRN dependency; SWI/SNF-deficient cells with SMARCA4 loss should show enhanced dependency on the SMARCA2 paralog; TP53-loss cells should show weaker MDM2 dependency because MDM2 inhibition is less effective when p53 is already inactive; and KEAP1-loss cells may be more dependent on NFE2L2 activity. For KRAS-mutant cells, I also expect weaker dependency on the related GTPase RIT1 because the direct KRAS oncogenic driver may reduce reliance on redundant RAS-family nodes. MYC amplification is used to probe replication/mitotic stress dependencies, with enhanced KIF18A dependency as an example. Finally, research marker F is tested as a constructed but potentially informative subgroup; if associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, it could define a candidate subgroup for follow-up, though it has no assigned biological role. All claims are initially unresolved and will be judged by effect size relative to clinical importance, uncertainty, and subgroup counts.

No new discovery evidence is attached in the current ledger: all registered claims (H1–H12) have empty evidence, and there are no assessments due. This appears to indicate that no analyses were requested/executed in the prior analyze step, rather than that results were obtained and found non-significant. Therefore I do not record evidence-based accept/reject assessments; all claims remain unresolved and active. No validation can be requested because no claims are eligible for validation. The prior proposal set is retained for later execution, but the immediate scientific status remains pending until the controller runs the registered comparisons and supplies estimates with uncertainty.

No independent validation results were delivered at this synthesis point, and there are no validation response deadlines for registered claims. The discovery evidence ledger remains empty for H1 through H12, so this absence of evidence is not evidence of no effect. Consequently, I support no accepted claims, negative findings, or validation conclusions at this time. All registered comparisons remain unresolved and active as pending tests rather than as null results. The most informative next analysis is to run the already registered discovery set H1-H12, which covers core oncogene-addiction hypotheses (KRAS, BRAF, EGFR, ERBB2), tumor-suppressor and DNA-repair/MRD contexts (TP53/MDM2, SMARCA4/SMARCA2, KEAP1/NFE2L2, MSI/WRN), pathway-redundancy expectations (KRAS-mutant RIT1 dependency), mitotic-stress hypotheses (MYC amplification/KIF18A), and a constructed marker probe (marker F/STAT3). After those estimates are available, I will prioritize follow-up where the signed effect is large relative to the clinical-threshold scale, the 95% interval is informative, subgroup cells are adequately populated, and the biological interpretation is coherent.

No discovery evidence has yet been generated for the initial claims, so I am not making evidence-based accept/reject assessments. The newly registered comparisons are hypothesis-driven but deliberately limited, to keep the immediate analysis budget focused on the original high-priority panel. For dependency_KRAS, I hypothesize that NF1 loss, which de-represses RAS signaling, will be associated with stronger KRAS dependency, giving a more negative exposed-minus-comparator contrast and therefore a negative signed effect. For dependency_WRN, I hypothesize that BRCA2 loss, a homologous-recombination defect, will associate with enhanced WRN dependency in a DNA-repair stress context. For dependency_USP7, I hypothesize the opposite sign: TP53-loss cells should be less dependent on USP7 because part of USP7's importance may be through protecting the p53 pathway; with TP53 loss exposed and wild-type comparator, a positive signed effect means weaker dependency in the loss group. For dependency_SMARCA2, ARID1A loss is another SWI/SNF chromatin-remodeling lesion, so I expect enhanced SMARCA2 dependency, analogous to the SMARCA4-loss paralog hypothesis but probing a different complex subunit. Finally, MYC amplification is used to probe transcriptional and translational addiction: high MYC output may make cells more sensitive to POLR2A, RPL11, and DHX9 depletion. These negative-direction claims correspond to more negative dependency scores, i.e., stronger dependency. All new claims are initially unresolved because no data have yet been supplied.

Requesting discovery analyses for the original high-priority panel H1-H12. These comparisons test the core oncogene-addiction and synthetic-lethality hypotheses in the lung cell-line dependency data: KRAS mutation and KRAS/BRAF/EGFR/ERBB2 dependencies, MSI-high/WRN, TP53 loss/MDM2, SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2, KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2, KRAS mutation/RIT1 redundancy, MYC amplification/KIF18A, and research marker F/STAT3. Running this set first will provide the necessary effect estimates, Welch intervals, and cell counts before deciding which comparisons to validate or refine.

The first discovery panel produced three unusually large effects and several small/null effects. Because all estimates are signed to the registered hypothesis direction, positive values support the original claim and negative values oppose it. H6 (MSI-high versus non-MSI on dependency_WRN, direction -1) has signed estimate +0.790 with 95% Welch interval +0.760 to +0.819 and cell counts 130 vs 1870. The raw contrast is therefore strongly negative: MSI-high cells show much stronger WRN dependency. This is several outcome SDs and far above a 10% relative scale, so I accept it. H8 (SMARCA4-loss versus SMARCA4-WT on dependency_SMARCA2, direction -1) has signed estimate +0.784 with interval +0.765 to +0.803 and balanced exposure n=412 vs 1588. This supports the synthetic-lethal paralog hypothesis and is robust in magnitude and sample size, so I accept it and request independent validation as the single most important confirmatory target. H9 (KEAP1-loss versus KEAP1-WT on dependency_NFE2L2, direction -1) has signed estimate -0.796 with interval -0.816 to -0.776; the raw contrast is positive, indicating weaker NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss cells, opposite to the registered prediction. I therefore reject the original H9 and register a reversed refinement for future testing/validation. The remaining effects are small relative to the dependency-score scale and do not justify acceptance. H3 is rejected because BRAF V600E did not show stronger BRAF dependency; the signed interval is compatible with a small opposite direction. H1 and H4 are biologically important but only borderline: H1 KRAS mutation/KRAS dependency and H4 EGFR amplification/EGFR dependency show point estimates in the predicted direction but intervals include null and near-null values, so they remain active unresolved. H2, H5, H7, H11, and H12 are small or imprecise; H2 interaction, H5 ERBB2 amplification, H7 TP53 loss/MDM2, and H11 MYC amplification/KIF18A are deferred as unresolved because their intervals leave room for small effects or competing directions, while H10 and H12 are rejected as clinically uninformative for their registered directions. Overall, H6 and H8 are the strongest dataset-level discoveries, while H9 reveals an unexpected reverse association needing a new hypothesis.

The independent validation for H8 is highly concordant with the discovery result. H8 is SMARCA4 loss versus SMARCA4 wild type on dependency_SMARCA2 with direction -1, so the reported signed estimate is +0.784 in discovery and +0.7925 in validation, meaning the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is strongly negative and the exposed SMARCA4-loss cells have much stronger SMARCA2 dependency. The validation interval is +0.7627 to +0.8223 at the stricter independent-validation level, with cell counts 391 and 1609, so the effect is precise, large, and far above any reasonable 10% clinical-significance scale on this dependency score. I therefore keep H8 accepted and close the original investigation as adequately established in this dataset, while not claiming causality or outside generalizability. I also reassess the reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 claim H20 using the parent evidence R9. H9 tested KEAP1 loss for stronger NFE2L2 dependency and was rejected because the raw contrast was positive. H20 has direction +1, and its displayed signed estimate is +0.796 with interval +0.776 to +0.816. This means KEAP1-loss cells show much weaker NFE2L2 dependency than KEAP1-WT cells in this dataset. The magnitude is huge relative to the outcome distribution, so I accept H20 as a dataset-level finding, but keep it active for possible independent validation and specificity checks. Among the remaining first-panel results, H6 remains accepted and active pending validation; H1 and H4 remain unresolved active because their point estimates are in the predicted oncogene-addiction direction but are only borderline relative to uncertainty and the 10% clinical scale; H2, H5, H7, and H11 remain deferred unresolved because their intervals are too wide or their effects too small to accept. H3, H10, H12, and the originally directed H9 remain closed negative findings.

I corrected the previous registration error by linking refinements only to claims with available motivating evidence. The accepted dataset-level findings are H6, H8, and H20, so the most informative refinements test whether their effects persist after restricting to technical, p53, MSI, or histology contexts. For H6, I registered the MSI-high versus WRN dependency effect within Avana-library screens and within TP53-intact screens to assess whether the huge WRN effect is robust and not driven by library or p53-loss context. For H8, I registered the validated SMARCA4-loss versus SMARCA2 effect within screen_batch and Avana-library subsets to test technical robustness. For H20, I registered the reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 effect in TP53-intact and MSI-intact subsets to test whether the unexpected weaker NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss cells persists in cleaner genomic contexts. The borderline KRAS and EGFR oncogene-addiction claims are refined to adenocarcinoma because these lesions are expected to be more dominant in that context. Finally, I added standalone specificity variants for NF1 loss on KRAS dependency within KRAS-mutation-free cells and BRCA2 loss on WRN dependency within MSI-intact cells; these are not marked as parent-linked refinements because the parent claims H13 and H14 currently have no evidence.

I selected 12 claims that produce new discovery evidence and prioritize the highest-value follow-up after H6, H8, and H20. The set tests three things. First, it completes the next core panel of biologically motivated predictor-outcome pairs: ARID1A loss with SMARCA2 dependency, NF1 loss with KRAS dependency, BRCA2 loss with WRN dependency, TP53 loss with USP7 dependency, and MYC amplification with POLR2A, RPL11, and DHX9 dependencies. These may reveal additional synthetic-lethal, pathway-redundancy, or transcriptional/translational dependency associations. Second, it tests robustness and specificity of the accepted MSI-high/WRN effect within Avana-library screens and TP53-intact screens. Third, it tests robustness and specificity of the accepted SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 effect within Avana-library screens and the KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 reversed effect within TP53-intact and MSI-intact screens. I deferred H23 because batch restriction is useful for technical robustness but library restriction is a stronger immediate specificity check for the SMARCA2 finding. I also deferred H27-H30 for now; if H13/H14/H17-H19 or the refinements are promising, those subtype or specificity variants can be prioritized next.

The new panel separates into one large new association, several strong robustness checks for prior accepted findings, and several near-null or opposite-direction effects. Because returned estimates are signed to each hypothesis direction, a positive signed estimate supports the registered claim. H15 is the key new discovery: TP53 loss versus TP53-intact screens for dependency_USP7 with direction +1 has signed estimate +0.396, 95% interval +0.325 to +0.467, n=406 vs 1594. Since direction +1 corresponds to a positive raw exposed-minus-comparator difference, TP53-loss cells show much weaker USP7 dependency (less negative scores) than TP53-intact cells. This is far above a 10% scale on the USP7 dependency distribution and is precise, so I accept H15 as a dataset-level association and request independent validation as the only voluntary validation this iteration. I did not validate H6 or H20 immediately despite their accepted status because their new subset analyses H21/H22/H25/H26 are highly concordant; H15 is a newly accepted claim with no independent confirmation yet and is therefore the higher-priority validation target. The MYC amplification panel is uninformative for the registered negative-direction hypotheses: H17 POLR2A signed estimate +0.004 with interval -0.017 to +0.025, H18 RPL11 signed estimate -0.012 with interval -0.034 to +0.009, and H19 DHX9 signed estimate -0.003 with interval -0.024 to +0.019 are all near null, and in each case the interval excludes a clinically meaningful effect in the predicted direction. I reject H17-H19 and close them. H13 NF1 loss/KRAS dependency signed estimate -0.020, interval -0.049 to +0.009, is small and opposite the predicted stronger KRAS dependency; because support is excluded beyond a clinically meaningful positive signed effect, I reject the overall H13 claim, though the already registered KRAS-mutation-free specificity variant H30 can remain for later review. H16 ARID1A loss/SMARCA2 dependency signed estimate -0.017, interval -0.057 to +0.023, does not support stronger SMARCA2 dependency; I reject the original H16 overall but register a refinement in SMARCA4-intact cells to test whether a weaker independent ARID1A effect can be detected once the dominant SMARCA4-loss effect is removed. H14 BRCA2 loss/WRN dependency is essentially null, signed estimate -0.0001, interval -0.045 to +0.045; the interval still includes positive support above the approximate 10% scale, so I defer rather than reject, pending the MSI-intact refinement H29. The robustness checks are strong: H21 MSI-high/WRN within Avana signed +0.794 interval +0.764 to +0.825; H22 within TP53-intact signed +0.780 interval +0.747 to +0.813; H24 SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 within Avana signed +0.781 interval +0.760 to +0.802; H25 KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 within TP53-intact signed +0.792 interval +0.770 to +0.815; H26 within MSI-intact signed +0.798 interval +0.777 to +0.819. These support H6, H8, and H20 without independent validation, but I still treat them as associations within this supplied dataset and not as causal or generalizable claims.

The H15 validation is highly concordant with discovery. H15 tests dependency_USP7 with TP53 loss versus TP53-intact screens under direction +1, so positive signed estimates mean the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is positive: TP53-loss cells have less negative USP7 scores and therefore weaker USP7 dependency. Discovery estimate was +0.396 (95% interval +0.325 to +0.467), n=406 vs 1594. Independent validation estimate was +0.395 with stricter interval +0.293 to +0.498 at alpha 0.003846, n=409 vs 1591. The validation interval excludes zero and a clinically trivial range, and the magnitude is approximately one SD of the dependency_USP7 distribution. Therefore I accept H15 and close its original investigation as a validated dataset-level association. I do not interpret this as proof that TP53 loss causally reduces USP7 dependency or that the association generalizes beyond this supplied dataset.

The current strongest supported findings in this dataset are: (1) MSI-high cells show markedly stronger WRN dependency than MSI-low/intact cells, H6 signed estimate +0.790 with interval +0.760 to +0.819; this persists within Avana-library screens, H21 +0.794 (+0.764 to +0.825), and within TP53-intact screens, H22 +0.780 (+0.747 to +0.813). (2) SMARCA4-loss cells show markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency, H8 discovery +0.784 and independent validation +0.792 (+0.763 to +0.822), with Avana-library support H24 +0.781. (3) KEAP1-loss cells show markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency, reversed from the original synthetic-lethal-like expectation; the accepted reversed claim H20 has signed estimate +0.796 (+0.776 to +0.816), and the effect persists in TP53-intact H25 +0.792 (+0.770 to +0.815) and MSI-intact H26 +0.798 (+0.777 to +0.819). These are dataset-level associations measured from predictor status and CRISPR dependency scores, not causal statements.

Negative or clinically uninformative findings include H3 BRAF V600E not showing stronger BRAF dependency, H10 KRAS mutation not showing RIT1 dependency, H12 research marker F not showing STAT3 dependency, H16 overall ARID1A loss not showing stronger SMARCA2 dependency, and the MYC amplification panel for POLR2A, RPL11, and DHX9 near or opposite to the predicted direction. H13 overall NF1 loss did not show the predicted stronger KRAS dependency. H14 BRCA2 loss was essentially null for WRN, but the MSI-intact refinement remains worth testing. Several unresolved items remain active because borderline effects or useful specificity checks have not yet been run: H1 KRAS mutation/KRAS dependency and H4 EGFR amplification/EGFR dependency are small but in the predicted direction, and their adenocarcinoma restrictions H27/H28 may determine whether the effects are context-specific or simply not clinically meaningful. H29 BRCA2 loss within MSI-intact screens and H30 NF1 loss within KRAS-mutation-free screens may refine the null overall effects. H31 will test whether the TP53-loss/USP7 association is robust within Avana-library screens. H32 will test whether ARID1A loss has an independent SMARCA2 dependency effect once SMARCA4-loss cells are removed; the newly proposed interaction will test whether ARID1A loss modifies SMARCA2 dependency within SMARCA4-loss versus SMARCA4-intact complement. I also propose testing CDKN2A loss for dependency_USP7 as a p53-pathway extension: if CDKN2A loss also associates with weaker USP7 dependency, that would broaden the biological context beyond TP53 loss; if null, it strengthens the interpretation that the observed association is specific to TP53-loss status in this dataset.

The most informative next analysis batch is to run the accepted-finding specificity checks and the new pathway refinements: H31 for USP7 technical robustness, the new CDKN2A/USP7 comparison, H32 and the new SMARCA2 interaction for ARID1A/SMARCA4 context, H27/H28 for KRAS and EGFR histologic specificity, and H29/H30 for BRCA2 and NF1 specificity. H23 batch restriction is deferred for now because library restriction H24 and validation have already provided strong technical robustness for H8. In a later appraise, the highest-value validation request should likely be H20 because its reversed direction is scientifically important and remains unvalidated, followed by H6 if capacity remains.

No assessments are due at this explore stage, so I am registering refinements that improve on the strongest accepted dataset-level findings and add a few focused, falsifiable new predictor-outcome hypotheses.

First, H6 remains an active accepted finding: MSI-high status is associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency (raw contrast strongly negative; signed estimate under direction -1 is about +0.79). The new refinement tests whether this remains clinically meaningful in the dominant adenocarcinoma subtype. Expected raw direction is still negative for MSI-high versus non-MSI-high, because WRN dependency is already robust overall, within Avana screens, and within TP53-intact screens; if the adenocarcinoma subset estimate remains large and negative, this strengthens the specificity of the accepted association for the main population of these lung screens. I also register an interaction of the MSI-high WRN effect by TP53 loss. Because the TP53-intact subset H22 was essentially as large as the overall effect, the most parsimonious expectation is little to no interaction: the MSI-high effect should not be materially stronger or weaker in TP53-loss screens. An interaction near zero would indicate the MSI-high WRN association is not driven by TP53 co-loss status. A large signed interaction would suggest context dependence and would justify further subgroup analysis.

Second, H20 remains the key accepted reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 finding: KEAP1-loss cells show markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency, accepted under direction +1. I add technical robustness within Avana-library screens and biological robustness within adenocarcinoma. The expected raw direction remains positive because the effect has already persisted in TP53-intact and MSI-intact subsets. I also add a TP53-loss interaction. Since KEAP1 and TP53 co-loss may occur in lung cancers, the TP53-loss interaction is an important specificity check: if KEAP1-loss versus KEAP1-intact NFE2L2 difference is similar with and without TP53 loss, the reversed association is more likely a direct or independent association rather than co-loss confounding. My initial expectation is roughly zero interaction because the TP53-intact subset effect was already nearly identical to the overall effect, but a positive interaction would still be scientifically interpretable as stronger weakening of NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss/TP53-loss contexts.

Third, H15 is accepted and validated: TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency under direction +1. I register a CDKN2A-intact refinement. CDKN2A loss often marks altered p53/RB pathway biology, so this tests whether the TP53-loss USP7 association persists when the more common CDKN2A-loss co-alteration is removed. Expected raw direction remains positive if the association is not merely a proxy for broader p53-pathway co-alteration. If the estimate shrinks toward zero, it suggests CDKN2A-loss or co-alteration structure may confound the TP53-loss association; if it remains large, H15 is more specific to TP53-loss status in this dataset.

Fourth, I add STK11-loss hypotheses for dependency_NFE2L2. STK11 is a lung tumor suppressor whose loss can co-occur with KEAP1/NFE2L2 pathway alterations, and KEAP1-loss already associates with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The overall STK11-loss hypothesis is direction +1, expecting less negative NFE2L2 scores in STK11-loss cells, with plausible alternatives being null if STK11 is unrelated or negative if STK11 loss creates stronger NFE2L2 dependency. Because co-occurrence with KEAP1 loss could drive an overall STK11 association, I also test STK11 loss only among KEAP1-loss-free cells. The anticipated raw direction there is near zero: if STK11's apparent effect is due to KEAP1 co-loss, it should disappear once KEAP1-loss cells are excluded. If a positive effect persists in KEAP1-loss-free cells, that would be evidence for an additional STK11-specific association in this dataset, not causal proof.

Finally, I add a WRN/TP53 main-effect check within MSI-intact screens. H22 established that MSI-high remains a strong WRN predictor among TP53-intact screens, but it does not directly test whether TP53 loss itself is associated with WRN dependency outside MSI-high context. This is a broad-exploration hypothesis with expected raw direction uncertain. If TP53 loss is associated with stronger WRN dependency, it could reveal additional replication-stress biology or confounding structure; if null, it clarifies that WRN dependency in MSI-intact screens is largely unrelated to measured TP53-loss status.

These proposals are dataset association tests. I am not assuming causality, mechanistic direction, or generalizability beyond the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR screens.

No assessments are due at the analyze stage, so I am selecting 12 previously registered claims that give the highest-value new discovery evidence. The batch has three priorities.

First, I focus on the two active accepted central findings that still lack independent validation: H6, MSI-high associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency, and H20, KEAP1 loss associated with markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency. For H6, H35 tests whether the MSI-high/WRN effect persists in the dominant adenocarcinoma subtype, and H36 tests whether the MSI-high effect is modified by TP53 loss. Together these address histologic context and p53 co-alteration context. For H20, H37 tests technical robustness within Avana-library screens, H38 tests robustness in adenocarcinoma, and H39 tests whether the KEAP1/NFE2L2 association is modified by TP53 loss. Because H20 has a large reversed effect, these specificity checks are important before accepting it as a broadly stable dataset-level association.

Second, I test the validated TP53/USP7 finding H15 for additional robustness and pathway specificity. H31 checks the TP53-loss effect within Avana-library screens, while H40 checks whether it persists among CDKN2A-intact cells. H33 tests CDKN2A loss itself as a predictor of weaker USP7 dependency. If CDKN2A loss shows a similar positive USP7 association, the p53-pathway context is broader; if CDKN2A loss is null but H40 remains positive, the validated association is more specific to TP53-loss status rather than CDKN2A-loss co-occurrence.

Third, I include focused new hypotheses and unresolved borderline claims. H41 tests STK11 loss as a predictor of weaker NFE2L2 dependency, and H42 tests STK11 loss among KEAP1-loss-free cells to determine whether any STK11 association is independent of the very large KEAP1-loss effect. This is biologically motivated by lung tumor-suppressor co-alteration patterns. H27 and H28 test KRAS-mutation/KRAS dependency and EGFR-amplification/EGFR dependency within adenocarcinoma, where oncogene-addiction effects might be more concentrated. These are useful because H1 and H4 were small but in the predicted direction overall and remain unresolved.

I defer H29/H30/H32/H34/H43 for this batch. H29 and H30 are refinements of near-null or rejected overall claims and are less urgent than central accepted findings and the new STK11 pathway hypothesis. H32/H34 test ARID1A/SMARCA2 context after the dominant SMARCA4-loss effect is established and after overall ARID1A was clinically uninformative. H43 tests TP53 loss on WRN among MSI-intact cells, but H36 already provides the most direct TP53 context check for the MSI-high/WRN effect. All analyses remain dataset association tests; causal or generalizable interpretation will be deferred.

The new results strongly support the already accepted central findings but leave most borderline or null extensions inconclusive. H31, H35, H37, H38, and H40 are large precise effects: TP53-loss is associated with much weaker USP7 dependency within Avana-library screens and within CDKN2A-intact screens; MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency in adenocarcinoma; KEAP1-loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency in Avana screens and adenocarcinoma. These are not independent validation samples, but they are strong internal specificity checks and I accept them as closed robustness confirmations. H27 and H28 remain clinically ambiguous: KRAS mutation and EGFR amplification show small positive signed differences in adenocarcinoma, but the point estimates are near the 10% clinical scale and the intervals include both no effect and a borderline clinically meaningful effect. I defer them rather than accept them. H33 is near-null for CDKN2A loss and USP7 dependency; because the interval still includes a possible clinically meaningful positive association, I leave it unresolved but low priority. H36 tests whether TP53 loss modifies the MSI-high WRN effect. The subgroup exposed cell has only 24 observations, and the interaction estimate is small with an interval crossing zero and extending into meaningful positive values, so it is inconclusive. H39 tests whether TP53 loss modifies the KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 effect; the estimate is near zero but not precise enough to claim no interaction, so I leave it unresolved and low priority. H41 and H42 provide no evidence that STK11 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency overall or in KEAP1-loss-free cells, but the intervals are not narrow enough to assert precise absence. I close these STK11 investigations as deprioritized inconclusive rather than as definitive nulls. I request independent validation for H20, the central reversed KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 association, because it is scientifically important and has not yet had independent validation. H6 has strong internal subset consistency and can wait until H20 validation is assessed.

The newly released validations substantially strengthen the central evidence set. H8 (SMARCA4 loss and stronger SMARCA2 dependency) now has both discovery and independent validation evidence: discovery signed estimate +0.784 (95% interval +0.765 to +0.803) and validation signed estimate +0.792 with a stricter interval +0.763 to +0.822. The magnitude is very large relative to the dependency_SMARCA2 scale and far above the 10% clinical-significance scale. I therefore accept H8 and close it as a validated dataset-level association. H20 (KEAP1 loss and weaker NFE2L2 dependency, the reversed-direction claim) is similarly strongly validated: discovery signed estimate +0.796 (+0.776 to +0.816) and validation signed estimate +0.806 (+0.775 to +0.838). This is a precise, large association and is consistent with earlier subset robustness checks. I accept H20 and close its primary investigation. Combined with previously validated H15, the strongest supported claims in the supplied dataset are now: SMARCA4-loss cells show much stronger SMARCA2 dependency; TP53-loss cells show much weaker USP7 dependency; KEAP1-loss cells show much weaker NFE2L2 dependency. These remain associations measured in the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR screens, not causal or externally generalizable claims. MSI-high versus MSI-intact remains an accepted active claim (H6) with very large internal effects, including Avana-library screens, TP53-intact screens, and adenocarcinoma, but it has not yet received the same independent validation treatment as H8, H15, and H20; it should be the next validation priority. Negative or clinically uninformative overall findings include BRAF V600E with BRAF dependency, KRAS mutation with RIT1 dependency, research marker F with STAT3 dependency, ARID1A loss overall with SMARCA2 dependency, MYC amplification with POLR2A/RPL11/DHX9 dependency, and NF1 loss with KRAS dependency. KRAS-mutation/KRAS-dependency and EGFR-amplification/EGFR-dependency remain small and borderline, including in adenocarcinoma, so they are not established as clinically meaningful. Interaction checks for TP53-loss modification of the MSI-high/WRN and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 effects are currently near-null but imprecise; the proposed new direct subset analyses test the exposed effects within TP53-loss screens, complementing the interactions. Next analyses should include these direct TP53-loss subset tests plus registered specificity checks such as BRCA2 loss within MSI-intact screens, NF1 loss among KRAS-mutation-free screens, ARID1A loss among SMARCA4-intact screens, the ARID1A/SMARCA4 interaction, and WRN association with TP53 loss among MSI-intact screens.

No assessments are due at this explore stage, so I am registering new comparisons that are mostly context-specific refinements of the strongest accepted associations plus a few targeted oncogene/p53 pathway follow-ups. The highest-priority scientific issue now is whether the large accepted dependencies are robust to common lung co-alteration structure rather than being driven by correlated genomic or clinical contexts. For SMARCA2, the accepted H8 effect is huge and validated, but TP53 loss is a common co-alteration in lung cancers; the new TP53-loss-only SMARCA4-loss test will show whether the SMARCA4-loss association remains clinically large when TP53 co-loss is present. If it remains near the overall magnitude, it supports an independent SMARCA4-loss association; if it shrinks sharply, co-alteration context becomes important. For KEAP1/NFE2L2, the accepted reversed effect H20 should be tested among STK11-intact screens. STK11 loss is common in lung tumors and can co-occur with KEAP1 loss; preservation of the KEAP1-loss effect in STK11-intact cells would make a direct STK11-co-loss explanation less plausible. For USP7, the accepted TP53-loss effect should be checked among MSI-intact screens to ensure it is not a MSI-high co-alteration artifact. For WRN, the MSI-high effect is already robust in TP53-intact and adenocarcinoma screens; I add STK11-intact testing because STK11 co-loss is another plausible co-alteration context. A large positive signed effect under direction -1 would indicate that MSI-high status remains a strong WRN predictor when STK11 loss is absent. I also register targeted checks for borderline receptor-tyrosine-kinase and p53 pathway effects: EGFR-amplified versus EGFR-wildtype dependency among TP53-intact screens, KRAS-mutant versus KRAS-wildtype dependency among STK11-intact screens, ERBB2-amplified versus ERBB2-wildtype dependency among TP53-intact screens, and TP53-loss versus TP53-intact MDM2 dependency among CDKN2A-intact screens. No assessments are due, so this explore stage registers follow-ups that should improve generalizability within the supplied dataset while testing a few scientifically plausible new associations. First, I add screen-batch robustness checks for three central validated associations: MSI-high/WRN, KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, and TP53-loss/USP7, restricted to batch_a. No new validation deadlines are open, so this synthesis consolidates the current evidence and allocates the next analyses. I use the supplied dataset-level framework: a signed lower bound above +0.10 is treated as evidence for a clinically meaningful association in the registered direction; a signed upper bound below +0.10 or an opposite-direction effect is treated as unsupported; intervals crossing +0.10 are treated as unresolved uncertainty rather than contradictions of the central result. All conclusions are associations within this lung-lineage CRISPR dataset and are not causal mechanisms or externally generalizable claims.

The five independently validated central associations are stable and large enough to support strong dataset-level conclusions. First, MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency: discovery H6 R6 signed effect +0.790 with 95% interval +0.760 to +0.819, and independent validation R52 +0.802 with strict interval +0.753 to +0.851. Because the claim direction is -1 on the dependency-score scale, this means a raw shift toward more negative WRN dependency scores, i.e. stronger dependency. This effect is far above the +0.10 benchmark and is robust across many tested technical and biological contexts, including libraries, batches, TP53 contexts, lineage subtype, STK11/CDKN2A contexts, and matched multimodal QC.

Second, SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency: discovery H8 R8 signed effect +0.784, interval +0.765 to +0.803; independent validation R13 +0.792, strict interval +0.763 to +0.822. This is a raw shift toward more negative SMARCA2 dependency scores. The effect is large and broadly consistent across multiple screened contexts, including batch, library, TP53, STK11, CDKN2A, and KY contexts.

Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, not stronger: the accepted reversal H20 has signed effect +0.796, interval +0.776 to +0.816, with independent validation R39 +0.806, strict interval +0.775 to +0.838. This corresponds to a raw shift toward less negative, i.e. weaker, NFE2L2 dependency scores. This is one of the most robust effects in the dataset across many subgroups and screen contexts.

Fourth, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency: H15 R17 signed +0.396, interval +0.325 to +0.467; validation R26 +0.395, strict interval +0.293 to +0.498. This is a raw shift toward less negative USP7 dependency scores, i.e. weaker dependency. The central effect is robust across Avana library, batch, matched QC, CDKN2A wild-type, MSI-negative, STK11-related, and MTAP-loss contexts. The KY-library context H80 is directionally supportive and was accepted only as borderline context evidence: discovery R73 lower bound +0.051, validation R91 strict lower bound +0.106 with wide uncertainty. This does not overturn the central TP53/USP7 association but should be reported as a less precise technical context.

Fifth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: H93 discovery R88 signed +0.267, interval +0.215 to +0.319; independent validation R90 +0.329, strict interval +0.255 to +0.402. Because the claim direction is -1, this is a raw shift toward more negative STAT3 dependency scores. The primary claim is independently supported. Robustness checks are now broadly consistent: batch_a H95 lower +0.125, adenocarcinoma H97 lower +0.206, matched RNA/DNA/CRISPR-QC H99 lower +0.221, PIK3CA-mutant H100 lower +0.127 with small exposed-cell caution, PIK3CA-wild-type H101 lower +0.210, and TP53-intact H103 lower +0.227. Two secondary contexts remain unresolved rather than contradictory: KY library H96 signed +0.158 but interval +0.063 to +0.254, and TP53-loss co-mutation context H102 signed +0.190, interval +0.085 to +0.296. These suggest context-specific precision loss, not evidence against the overall validated PTEN/STAT3 association.

The negative evidence is also informative. Many biologically motivated direct-target or pathway hypotheses were rejected because their signed intervals either crossed zero or remained well below the +0.10 benchmark, or moved in the opposite direction. These include KRAS mutation as a predictor of KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E as a predictor of BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification as a predictor of EGFR dependency, ERBB2 amplification as a predictor of ERBB2 dependency, MYC amplification against KIF18A, POLR2A, RPL11, DHX9, and TMED10, BRCA2 loss against WRN, DHX9, and POLR2A, ARID1A loss against SMARCA2, STK11 loss against TMED10 and NFE2L2 contexts, MTAP loss against USP7 or MDM2 in most contexts, PIK3CA mutation against STAT3, RB1 loss against KIF18A, and the constructed research markers D, E, and F across WRN, SMARCA2, USP7, NFE2L2, and STAT3. These are best described as unsupported dataset-level hypotheses within the tested comparisons, not proof of absence.

The next most informative work is to resolve whether the new PTEN/STAT3 association is modified by major co-mutation architecture, especially KRAS and TP53 context. The already active subgroup means H107 and H108 are valuable, and I have now registered an interaction of PTEN-loss/STAT3 dependency by KRAS mutation and another by TP53 loss to ask the sharper effect-modification question. I also registered a TP53-loss/USP7 interaction by KEAP1 loss to test whether a central oxidative-stress co-mutation context changes the otherwise robust TP53/USP7 association. The existing active RB1-loss POLR2A probe H109 remains useful as a final targeted discovery screen. If these analyses produce a new robust effect with lower bound above +0.10, it should be accepted as a dataset-level association and considered for independent validation; if they produce wide crossing intervals, they should be reported as unresolved; if they produce nulls, they should be closed as unsupported. No validation request is warranted now because the central associations have already been independently validated and the remaining questions are either robustness or exploratory effect modification.

No assessments are due, so this exploration adds refinements that fit alongside the already active H107-H112 analyses while leaving enough analyze capacity for a targeted but not redundant discovery screen. The central independently validated dataset-level associations remain MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency, and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. The next analyses should mainly test whether these findings are robust under high-quality multimodal profiling, major subtype context, and biologically interpretable co-condition or co-mutation contexts, plus a small number of new pathway probes. For signed mean differences, I will treat a lower bound above +0.10 as clinically meaningful support in the registered direction, an upper bound below +0.10 as unsupported, and intervals crossing +0.10 as unresolved context-specific uncertainty. For interactions, the same benchmark applies to the interaction estimate: a signed lower bound above +0.10 supports effect modification in the registered direction, while an interval crossing +0.10 does not establish modification.

First, I register the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2-dependency association in the matched RNA/DNA plus CRISPR-QC subset as a refinement of H8. This is the most direct way to test whether the large synthetic-lethal pattern survives in cells with complete multimodal profiling. Expected raw direction: SMARCA4-loss cells have more negative dependency_SMARCA2 scores than SMARCA4-intact cells; signed to direction -1, I anticipate a positive estimate. Alternatives include a null technical/selection context, an attenuated effect if profiling subset differs systematically, or an effect smaller than the clinical benchmark because of residual confounding.

Second, I register the KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2-dependency reversal in the matched RNA/DNA plus CRISPR-QC subset as a refinement of H20. This central effect is very large: KEAP1 loss associates with weaker, less negative NFE2L2 dependency. Testing it in high-quality profiles asks whether the reversal is an assay artifact or a stable dataset-level association. Expected raw direction is positive, i.e. KEAP1-loss cells have less negative NFE2L2 scores than KEAP1-intact cells.

Third, I register the TP53-loss/USP7-dependency association specifically in adenocarcinoma as a refinement of H15. TP53/USP7 has been robust across many technical and co-mutation strata, but not directly in the largest lineage_subtype category. The expected raw direction remains positive because the accepted central finding is that TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency. This is a robustness probe rather than a new mechanism; if it clears +0.10, it strengthens the subtype-level consistency of the association.

Fourth, I register an interaction of PTEN-loss/STAT3-dependency effect by media_serum_pct=10. PTEN loss may alter STAT3 dependence through growth-factor, PI3K/AKT, and inflammatory signaling. High serum could amplify ligand-driven STAT3 crosstalk and make PTEN-loss cells more STAT3 dependent, but it could also supply survival signals that buffer the dependence, so this remains falsifiable and biologically interpretable. The raw hypothesis is that the PTEN-loss effect is more negative in high-serum screens than in the same eligible population outside high serum; I signed the interaction to direction -1. Alternatives include no effect modification, a weaker PTEN-loss effect in high serum, or an interaction in the opposite direction.

Finally, I add two modest new pathway probes rather than repeating the many closed direct-target nulls. First, APC-mutant cells may depend more strongly on TMED10 because APC loss rewires Wnt signaling and TMED10 contributes to cargo trafficking/Wnt secretion; the hypothesis is a raw more-negative TMED10 dependency in APC-mutant cells. Second, SMAD4 loss may alter inflammatory and TGF-beta-associated states, potentially increasing STAT3 dependence through compensatory signaling; the hypothesis is a raw more-negative dependency_STAT3 in SMAD4-loss cells. These new probes are not motivated by prior accepted effects, so a null would only close these specific hypotheses within this supplied dataset, not prove absence in external data.

All new claims are dataset-level association tests. They do not establish causality, therapeutic relevance, or generalizability beyond this supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset. I do not request validation in this stage because no new robust discovery has yet emerged from the current active battery.

The open validation deadlines were for the PTEN-loss/STAT3-dependency association (H93) and the KY-library TP53-loss/USP7-dependency context (H80). H80 remains a narrower technical-context claim: TP53 loss versus USP7 dependency within KY-library screens. The central evidence map is now stable. The independently supported dataset-level associations are: MSI-high associated with stronger WRN dependency; SMARCA4 loss associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency; KEAP1 loss associated with weaker, not stronger, NFE2L2 dependency; TP53 loss associated with weaker USP7 dependency; and PTEN loss associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. Many biologically motivated direct-target and pathway hypotheses remain unsupported, including KRAS mutation as a predictor of KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E for BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification for EGFR dependency, ERBB2 amplification for ERBB2 dependency, MYC amplification across several dependencies, BRCA2 loss across WRN/DHX9/POLR2A, ARID1A loss for SMARCA2, RB1 loss for KIF18A or POLR2A, APC mutation for TMED10, SMAD4 loss for STAT3, and the constructed research markers. The main remaining uncertainty is context-specific effect modification and precision in secondary subgroups. The PTEN/STAT3 interaction by TP53 loss was rejected because the signed interaction upper bound was below the benchmark. Other PTEN/STAT3 context interactions remain unresolved but are not strong contradictions: KRAS mutation modification, media-serum modification, and PIK3CA interaction have point estimates near zero and intervals crossing the benchmark. Secondary PTEN/STAT3 means in the KY library and TP53-loss context remain borderline/unresolved. KEAP1-loss modification of TP53/USP7 is also unresolved. I have deferred these secondary interaction questions rather than spending further discovery effort on them now.

For the next analyses, I prioritize focused robustness probes of central associations in biologically interpretable co-mutation or culture contexts, rather than repeating accepted direct-target nulls. I register: SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2 in adenocarcinoma; KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2 in MTAP-loss context; TP53 loss/USP7 in STK11-loss context; and PTEN loss/STAT3 in STK11-loss, KEAP1-loss, MTAP-loss, and high-serum culture contexts.
